schedule.implemented_in: harness-v4/arm_ev.py (worst_case + xtrack2.capacity before each project-arm batch)
schedule.rule: before a project-arm batch: the project's rolling 24 h capacity (60 minus every track's requests in the last 24 h, the A base included) must cover the batch's worst case (the remaining durable allowance, 12 minus charged, of every pending PDF); otherwise the project is persisted as deferred for that arm and zero requests are sent; a later resume takes deferred projects in declared order (arms in the frozen order, projects by EP, documents in stage order)
schedule.simulator: harness-v4/schedule_sim.py (hourly steps; a batch's requests are charged to the window at its start; arms strictly in order, each arm over all projects before the next)
assumptions: each arm's batch for a project sends its whole demand at the batch start (the real batch spreads over its run time, so real windows free up later, never earlier)
sequential requests at the observed p50 latencies; the run time of a batch is NOT added to the window arithmetic (reported separately)
no failures, timeouts, tripwire stops or cap refusals; a cap refusal only shortens a batch
the A base's requests are either aged out (L1 starts >= 24 h after A) or its cap of 8 is spent on the largest project at t = 0

schedule.note: elapsed hours are to the START of the last batch; add that batch's run time; nothing here is a completion guarantee
schedule.pairs_first: L1 and L2 are completed (or deferred per project) before L3 and L4, so the ROI contrast is complete first; within an arm, projects in EP order, documents in stage order
schedule.incomplete_pairs: a document an arm could not attempt (deferred beyond the run window, share refusal, cap, breaker) stays in the all-planned denominator as not_attempted / budget for that arm; each pair's analysis reports (a) all planned, (b) documents attempted by both arms of the pair, (c) field-specific read-in-both sets, all with document IDs; a pair with fewer than 12 attempted-by-both documents is reported INCONCLUSIVE
schedule.r21_table_correction: R21 reported 'worst case 3 days / expected 2 days' from a rounded rule of thumb; the simulated figures above replace them
